exercises.name: Dead-hang on Jugs
exercises.description: Dead-hang on jug holds for warm-up and endurance.

exercises.name: Max finger strength
exercises.description: Max finger strength (usually half-crimp) weighted hangs (90-100% of your maximum). Hangboard exercise designed to increase the maximum force your fingers can produce. Stop if grip position breaks down. For weaker climbers the same exercise can be done with assistance (e.g. pulley/band) to reach the appropriate intensity.

exercises.name: Push-ups
exercises.description: Standard push-ups for antagonist training.

exercises.name: Strength Endurance Hangboard
exercises.description: Hangboard strength-endurance protocol using repeated 7-second hangs with 3 seconds of rest. Use a moderate-high intensity that allows all repetitions with controlled grip position.

exercises.name: 2on 2off
exercises.description: 2 minutes on the wall, 2 minutes off the wall. No hard pump. Primarily aerobic/low-intensity endurance training.

exercises.name: Easy Routes Autobelay
exercises.description: Easy routes on autobelay for aerobic endurance.

exercises.name: Simon Fryer 2016 Endurance Protocol
exercises.description: Simon Fryer's endurance protocol (2016) for sustained climbing capacity (50-60%).  Use a comfortable, deep edge (typically 20mm-30mm) in a half-crimp or open-hand position. Remove weight using a pulley system or keep your feet on the floor so you are only taking 30% to 40% of your maximum capacity. It should feel exceptionally light.

exercises.name: Fryer on Routes (Linked Laps)
exercises.description: Fryer-style aerobic endurance on routes: climb up, lower, immediately back on for 2-3 consecutive laps on easy terrain (50-60% intensity, never approaching pump). 2 sets, each set is 8-12 minutes of continuous climbing. Rest 5 min between sets. Focus on breathing, pace, and relaxed movement throughout.

exercises.name: Easy Routes with Shake-out Practice
exercises.description: 5 routes with 3 min rest between at 2-3 grades below redpoint level. On each route, deliberately stop at every good rest to practice shake-outs (30-60 seconds per arm). Focus on finding efficient rest positions, controlled breathing, and full forearm recovery before continuing. Never approach pump — the goal is building the skill of mid-route recovery on easy terrain.

exercises.name: Stretching
exercises.description: Full body stretching session focused on shoulders, hips, and forearms.

exercises.name: Outdoor Climbing
exercises.description: Outdoor climbing session on rock.

exercises.name: Bouldering
exercises.description: 1 hour bouldering session on boards or in gym. Focus on quality movement and trying hard problems.

exercises.name: Kenees Program
exercises.description: Knee rehabilitation/prehab program.

exercises.name: On-Wall ARC Intervals
exercises.description: Aerobic Restitution and Capillarity (ARC) training for continuous climbing capacity. Move continuously on very easy holds at ~40% MVC. Forearms should feel light heat or a mild warm feeling, but never a full pump. Progress weekly by extending set duration rather than increasing wall difficulty.

exercises.name: Warm-up Paradigm Climbing
exercises.description: Progressive climbing warm-up: 2 min jumping jacks (easy cardio), arm circles/leg swings/finger movement (tendon glides), scapular pull-ups/asymmetric lock-offs/progressive hangs/easy climbing, quick dead-points/explosive pull-ups.

exercises.name: Shoulder Isometric
exercises.description: Shoulder Isometric 30 sec

exercises.name: Repeaters (Hangboard)
exercises.description: Hangboard repeater protocol: 7 seconds on / 3 seconds off for 6-8 reps per set. Use an edge size and load that produces significant pump by the final rep but allows controlled grip throughout. Trains the forearm's ability to sustain force output under fatigue — a key capacity for sustained hard route climbing.

exercises.name: Rope Power Endurance Laps
exercises.description: Climb 2-3 consecutive laps on a routes climbing wall near flash level without resting (lowered quickly or pulled back up immediately), then rest 8-10 minutes between sets. Trains fatigue resistance and sustained hard execution under severe pump.

exercises.name: Power Endurance Circuits
exercises.description: Link 3-4 boulder problems at flash level back-to-back without rest, then rest 4-5 minutes. Trains the ability to sustain hard climbing when pumped. Equivalent to 4x4s.
3-4 sets of max hangs before climbing. Focus on form, half-crimp position.
Work problems at your limit or 1 grade below. Focus on quality attempts with full rest.
Antagonist work at end of session.
4 sets of 7on/3off repeaters. Use an edge that produces solid pump by rep 6-7. 5 min rest between sets. Half-crimp position.
3 rounds of 4 boulder problems linked back-to-back. 5 min rest between rounds.
Linked route laps on easy terrain. Continuous movement for 8-12 minutes per set.
6 rounds of 2 min on / 2 min off. Easy climbing, no hard pump.
4-5 easy routes with deliberate shake-out practice on moderate sections.
Project session or redpoint attempts on target-grade routes.
Volume day: climb many routes below your max. Build mileage and work on technique outdoors.
Easy climbing at end of day for recovery and capillarity.
